title: Unify common-corpus loader: index.js vs lambda-index.js
description:
package.json main=index.js means require('common-corpus') always loads index.js, never lambda-index.js, in any environment. index.js's uncompress() unzips corpus .zip/.7z files into path.join(__dirname, './unzip-temp') — under Lambda, __dirname resolves inside the read-only /opt layer mount, so any corpus text still packaged as .zip/.7z throws (EROFS/EACCES) on first read in prod while working locally.

Currently dormant, not live: verified libs/common-corpus/corpus/ has zero .zip/.7z files today (120 .txt, 4 .js, ~89MB) — the unzip branch never fires. It's a landmine left from the Heroku-era strategy (unzip-on-first-request, cache to disk across a dyno's up-to-24h life, done to fit more texts under Heroku slug-size limits) that structurally cannot work under Lambda even once: /opt is read-only regardless of invocation count, unlike Heroku's writable/persistent dyno fs. Also, Lambda layers allow up to 250MB unzipped (function+layers combined) — current 89MB uncompressed corpus doesn't need the zip strategy for space reasons either.

lambda-index.js is a correct-in-spirit Lambda-safe rewrite (env-aware path via AWS_LAMBDA_FUNCTION_NAME, no on-the-fly unzip, LRU cache) but is dead code — nothing requires it — AND has its own bug: its isLambda path points at /opt/nodejs/node_modules/common-corpus/corpus-extracted, but build:layer:prepare only copies corpus/ into the layer, never a corpus-extracted dir. That mismatch needs fixing too (or just point it at corpus/ directly since nothing needs pre-extraction anymore).

Fix: make one loader env-aware (fix the corpus-extracted path mismatch) and delete the other; don't patch index.js in place. Low urgency in practice since dormant, but landmine for whoever next adds an archived corpus text.
design:
Resolution plan (agreed with user 2026-08-08):

Don't just keep index.js. Once uncompress() is deleted, index.js's only reason to differ from lambda-index.js disappears — and the read-only-/opt constraint that made index.js Lambda-hostile was specifically about *writing* (mkdirp + zipkit.unzipSync into unzip-temp/). Plain fs.readFileSync against a path under /opt is fine; layers are read-only, not unreadable. So build the survivor off lambda-index.js's shape, not index.js's.

Concrete changes:
1. Delete uncompress()/unzipLoc block entirely (index.js) and the now-pointless isLambda-zip-skip branch in walkSync (lambda-index.js) — no corpus file is zipped (verified: 0 .zip/.7z in corpus/, 120 .txt + 4 .js).
2. Fix lambda-index.js's getCorpusPath(): currently points at /opt/nodejs/node_modules/common-corpus/corpus-extracted, but build:layer:prepare only ever copies corpus/ — never a corpus-extracted dir. Either drop the '-extracted' suffix, or simpler: drop the Lambda-specific branch entirely and use path.join(__dirname, './corpus') unconditionally in all environments (works under /opt now that nothing writes). Keep the CORPUS_PATH env override for local/test flexibility.
3. Keep lambda-index.js's good parts: correct cleanName regex (closes textgen-monorepo-bez for free), LRU textCache/getCachedText (addresses the separately-flagged 'walks 89MB corpus every invocation' perf smell), per-file try/catch resilience in the walk/load loops.
4. Consolidate to a single file. Simplest: keep the name index.js (package.json main already points there, no need to touch main) but with lambda-index.js's logic. Delete lambda-index.js.
5. Drop node-zipkit and mkdirp from package.json dependencies — grepped, used only inside index.js's uncompress path, nowhere else in the repo. Bonus: rimraf is also listed as a dependency and is unreferenced anywhere in source — unrelated dead weight, drop it too while touching this file.
6. Update build:layer:prepare script: currently copies 'corpus/ index.js lambda-index.js package.json' into the layer — drop lambda-index.js from that list.
7. Remove stale comment in test/corpora.provider.tests.js:10 ('setup should make sure that the unzip-temp folder is empty') — no actual zip fixtures in tests, just this comment.

Approach: TDD. Corpus loading currently has thin test coverage (flagged separately) — write tests first for the consolidated loader (path resolution across CORPUS_PATH/default, cleanName correctness, cache behavior, per-file error resilience) before changing implementation.

Closes textgen-monorepo-bez (cleanName regex) as a side effect of consolidation.
close_reason: Consolidated to single index.js: removed uncompress/zip logic (node-zipkit, mkdirp deps dropped), fixed getCorpusPath to work identically local/Lambda via CORPUS_PATH env override + __dirname-relative default, kept lambda-index.js's LRU cache + per-file resilience, deleted lambda-index.js. TDD: 14 new tests in test/corpus-loader.tests.js, all passing.

title: Fix cleanName regex bugs in libs/common-corpus/index.js
description: Line 55: extension-strip regex /.(txt|js|zip)$/g is unescaped (matches any char before extension, eats one extra char); separator-strip regex /^\/|\\/ is mis-anchored, parses as (^\/)|(\\) so the backslash branch is unanchored and strips a mid-string backslash anywhere. lambda-index.js:128-130 already has the correct escaped versions — backport them into index.js, the file actually loaded (see main:index.js in package.json).
close_reason: Fixed as part of ax8 consolidation: cleanName now uses /\.(txt|js)$/gi (escaped dot, case-insensitive) and /^[/\\]/ (properly anchored separator strip). Verified against real corpus's SWSECOND.TXT (previously mismatched due to case-sensitivity).

title: Fix pickRemove random-seed misuse in apps/poeticalbot/src/lib/util.js
description: Line 72: math.random(arr.length) — random-seed's math.random() takes no args, so the arg is ignored and it returns a float in [0,1), truncated to index 0 by splice. pickRemove always removes index 0, never random. corporaSevenStrategy calls this 7x expecting a random sample of corpus texts but always gets the first 7 in array order.
close_reason: Fixed math.random(arr.length) -> math(arr.length) in pickRemove (src/lib/util.js:73). random-seed's math.random() takes no args and ignores them, returning a float in [0,1) that splice() truncates to index 0 — pickRemove always removed the first element, never random. TDD: added test/util.tests.js 'functional tests' block (the file had a literal 'TODO: okay, now actually test the methods!' — addressed for pickRemove) with a seeded deterministic test (seed 'test-seed', 5-element array) computed against random-seed's real API, watched it fail with the exact always-index-0 pattern before fixing. Verified 272 passing / 1 pre-existing unrelated failure in the unit suite.

title: Stop logging Tumblr API credentials in apps/listmania/index.js
description: Line 60: config object (consumerKey/consumerSecret/accessToken/accessSecret) is passed to console.log(JSON.stringify(config)) on every successful run. Leaks live Tumblr secrets into stdout/CloudWatch logs. One-line fix: remove or redact before logging.
close_reason: Removed the console.log(JSON.stringify(config)) at index.js:60 that dumped consumerKey/consumerSecret/accessToken/accessSecret in plaintext on every successful list generation. Verified no regressions in listmania's util/textutil suites.

title: Generate Lambda package.json from real package.json instead of bash heredoc
description: apps/poeticalbot/build-lambda.sh and apps/listmania/build-lambda.sh both hand-author a Lambda package.json via heredoc, duplicating the real dependency list. Already caused real drift: poeticalbot's build-lambda.sh hardcodes tumblr.js ^3.0.0 while local package.json uses ^5.0.0 — deployed Lambda runs a different major version than what's developed/tested. Both scripts also hardcode node 18.x engines while real package.json specifies ^22.16.0/22.x, and both run npm install --production in the temp dir, bypassing the pnpm lockfile the repo treats as authoritative. Fix: derive the Lambda package.json programmatically from the source package.json (filter workspace deps, keep versions) instead of hand-maintaining a second copy.
close_reason: Added scripts/generate-lambda-package-json.js: derives Lambda package.json from the app's real package.json (drops workspace:* deps served via Lambda layer, keeps real dep versions + engines), replacing both apps' hand-authored heredocs. Fixes the drift bug directly: poeticalbot's tumblr.js now correctly ^5.0.0 (was hardcoded ^3.0.0) and node engine ^22.16.0 (was 18.x); listmania's node engine now 22.x (was 18.x). Wired into both build-lambda.sh scripts, ran both end-to-end (npm install + zip) successfully, standard lint clean.

title: Bound retry loops in apps/poeticalbot/src/lib/poetifier.js
description: Line 185: letterExistsFilterTransform's while loop re-rolls a random target letter with no iteration cap — an unlucky run can spin for a long time inside a Lambda invocation with fixed timeout, burning billed duration or timing out. Line 275: title-retry do/while's exit condition (poem.title.split(' ').length === 0) can never be false since String.split always returns length >= 1 — the loop runs exactly once regardless of a degenerate/blank title, so the intended retry never happens.
close_reason: Extracted both buggy retry loops into src/lib/retry-bounds.js (boundedLetterFilter, retryTitle) for testability, TDD'd 5 tests in test/retry-bounds.tests.js, wired both back into poetifier.js. letterExistsFilterTransform now caps at 25 attempts instead of spinning unbounded on a scarce/absent letter. Title retry now actually checks for a blank title (trim().length===0 instead of the always-false split().length===0) and caps at 10 attempts instead of running exactly once regardless. 248 unit tests pass (1 pre-existing flaky unseeded-random test unrelated to this change, confirmed flaky before/after).

title: Add validation depth to npf-formatter.js (empty content array passes)
description: validateNPF (line 167) only checks content is an array, never that it's non-empty. A poem with no title and no text produces content: []; validation returns true and tumblr-client.js posts an empty NPF post live instead of failing loudly.
close_reason: validateNPF now rejects empty content arrays (npf-formatter.js:168). TDD: added failing test in test/npf-formatting.tests.js confirming empty poem -> content:[] passed validation, then fixed check to length===0 -> false. Both real callers (src/index.js, tumblr-client.js) already throw/reject on false, so this closes the live-post-empty-post hole. 243 unit tests pass.

title: poeticalbot: lambda-handler.js has same config.poetry nesting bug as cli.js (pre-cai fix)
description: lambda-handler.js's generatePoem() (lines ~213-240) nests CLI/message overrides under generationConfig.poetry.{method,seed,corporaFilter}, identical to the bug fixed in cai for cli.js. Poetifier.js reads these top-level (config.method/seed/corporaFilter/transform), so Lambda-invoked overrides are silently ignored the same way CLI ones were. Also missing the transform override entirely (cli.js had it, lambda-handler.js does not). Apply the same top-level fix.

title: poeticalbot: CLI overrides (--method/--corpora-filter/--seed/--transform) are silent no-ops (config.poetry nesting mismatch)
description:
Root cause found (2026-08-24), bigger than originally scoped: cli.js's generatePoem() nests all CLI overrides under generationConfig.poetry.{method,corporaFilter,seed,transform} (src/cli.js ~lines 117-140). But config.js's base config object has no `poetry` key at all, and poetifier.js reads `config.method`, `config.corporaFilter`, `config.seed`, `config.transform` etc. at the TOP level (`let config = options.config`, src/lib/poetifier.js:21, then config.corporaFilter/config.method/... used directly, never config.poetry.*).

Net effect: --method, --corpora-filter, --seed, and --transform are silently ignored end-to-end — Poetifier always falls through to its own internal random method/corpus selection (the hardcoded corporaFilterStrategy(...) list in poetifier.js's reduceCorpora). Only --post, --verbose, --help actually work as CLI flags.

Confirmed empirically: `node src/cli.js --method queneau-buckets --corpora-filter eliot --verbose` produced method "jgnoetry" and Source files from egyptian/lincoln/spam corpora, not eliot.

Originally filed narrower (just --corporaFilter vs --corpora-filter flag-name mismatch in cli.js's own arg parser) - that half is real too and now fixed (cli:sample script corrected, no more "Unknown option" warnings), but doesn't matter much since the value never reached poetifier.js anyway due to this nesting bug.

Not fixed as part of this session's smoke-test work — cli:sample was simplified to plain `node src/cli.js --verbose` (drops the non-functional --method/--corpora-filter flags rather than leave them looking functional) so the smoke test doesn't depend on this bug being fixed. This bead is now about the deeper fix: make CLI overrides actually reach Poetifier.
acceptance_criteria:
- --method queneau-buckets reliably forces queneau-buckets (verify via --verbose output's "method" field)
- --corpora-filter eliot reliably restricts Source to eliot-matching corpus files
- --seed and --transform overrides also verified reaching Poetifier
- Either: poetifier.js reads config.poetry.* to match cli.js's nesting, OR cli.js is changed to set top-level config.* to match poetifier.js — pick one consistent contract, document it

title: poeticalbot: bump compromise v11->14, audit pattern-match.js tag DSL
description:
apps/poeticalbot depends on compromise@^11.13.2. Its src/lib/pattern-match.js builds a match-template DSL against a hardcoded list of ~55 compromise tag names (Adjective, Noun, Copula, NounPhrase+, etc.) plus POS accessors (.nouns(), .verbs(), etc.) and .match(template).out('array').

Research (2026-08-23) found:
- .match().out('array') and POS accessors are confirmed stable/unchanged in current compromise docs — not the risk.
- The tag list itself is the risk: of the 55 tags in pattern-match.js, ~9 (16%) are already questionable independent of any version bump — `Auxillary` is a plain typo (real tag is `Auxiliary`, so that template branch has likely been a silent no-op since it was written), and ClauseEnd/Contraction/FuturePerfect/NiceNumber/Pluperfect/Quotation/RelativeDay don't appear in current compromise docs at all. NounPhrase+/VerbPhrase+ status unclear — may already be dead in v11 too.
- Recommendation from research: do NOT bump versions first. Build a baseline first — run all 55 tags against the CURRENTLY INSTALLED v11 to see what already matches vs. silently no-ops. That baseline is the only way to know true blast radius of a version bump. textgen-monorepo-ap7 (pattern-match REPL tool) is the intended vehicle for that baseline.

Also touches: apps/poeticalbot/src/lib/transformations.js, lrRunner.js, metaphone.js, linereduce.js, textutil.js — all reference compromise, not yet individually audited.

Depends conceptually on textgen-monorepo-ap7 (REPL) for the baseline step, though not a hard blocker if baseline is done ad-hoc instead.
acceptance_criteria:
- Baseline established: which of the 55 tags in pattern-match.js actually match anything under v11 today
- package.json dependency bumped from compromise@^11.13.2 to compromise@^14.16.0 (or documented reason for a different target)
- Re-run baseline against new version, diff against v11 baseline, fix/remove regressed templates
- poeticalbot test suite passes (nx test poeticalbot)

title: common-corpus: replace nlp_compromise@6.5.3 with compromise@14.16.0 (sentencify rewrite)
description:
common-corpus's lib/textutil.js sentencify() is the only user of nlp_compromise (6.5.3, ancient pre-rename package). Usage is tiny: `nlp.text(t).sentences.map(s => s.str.trim())`.

title: Interactive REPL for testing pattern-match templates against corpus
description:
No fast way to iterate on compromise match templates (see apps/poeticalbot/src/lib/pattern-match.js) against real corpus text. Currently the only way to see what a template like '#Adjective #Noun of #Noun' actually matches is to run a full poeticalbot generation cycle.

Want a standalone REPL/CLI tool: load a corpus file (or category via common-corpus), type a match template or POS-accessor call, see matched fragments immediately. Should reuse pattern-match.js's matchStrategyFactory/posStrategy logic rather than reimplementing it.

Two direct uses:
- textgen-monorepo-vyv (modernize common-corpus toolchain, incl. nlp_compromise->compromise bump): lets us manually verify pattern-match.js's ~55-tag DSL still matches the same way after a compromise version bump, before trusting it in the full pipeline.
- textgen-monorepo-cet (new 'noun, state' list-poem style): needs to explore how nouns pair with participles/states in corpus text — this tool is exactly the exploration surface for designing that pairing logic.
acceptance_criteria:
- Can point at a corpus source (file path or common-corpus category filter) and get a loaded text/sentence set
- Can enter a compromise match template or call a POS accessor (nouns/adjectives/verbs/etc.) and see matched output live, without restarting
- Reuses pattern-match.js's matching logic (not a parallel reimplementation)

title: poeticalbot: src/lambda-handler.js API mismatch breaks Lambda Handler Integration test
description:
test/lambda-handler.tests.js does 'const { handler } = require("../src/lambda-handler")' expecting an object with a handler function, but src/lambda-handler.js exports the LambdaHandler CLASS directly ('module.exports = LambdaHandler'), so the destructured 'handler' is undefined and the test's before-all hook throws 'TypeError: handler is not a function'.

Discovered while running the full test suite (npm test / test:js) during textgen-monorepo tg-4 (Prettier swap) -- test:unit's --invert --grep 'integration|Integration' filter always excluded this file, so it's been silently broken and never caught by the normal per-commit verification loop.

Separately, src/index.js ALSO defines its own standalone 'exports.handler = async (event, context) => {...}' (self-contained, does NOT use the LambdaHandler class at all), and that's the one actually wired up as the real entry point (package.json main=src/index.js, build-lambda.sh copies src/* verbatim). So src/lambda-handler.js's LambdaHandler class appears to be a parallel/abandoned implementation that nothing in production actually calls -- needs investigation into whether it should be wired up (and the test fixed to match) or deleted as dead code, consistent with poeticalbot's ongoing src/ consolidation (see .kiro/specs/codebase-consolidation).
close_reason: Root cause: test/lambda-handler.tests.js was a stray unreferenced dupe of test/integration/lambda-handler.tests.js, pointing at wrong module shape (destructured {handler} from src/lambda-handler.js, which exports the LambdaHandler class directly, not a handler fn). Deleted the stray file -- the correct integration test (against src/index.js's exports.handler, the real prod entry) already exists at test/integration/lambda-handler.tests.js. Also confirmed the bead's dead-code hypothesis was wrong: src/index.js DOES delegate to LambdaHandler class (line 125), so it's live prod code, not orphaned. test:js suite: 280 passing, 0 failing.

title: poeticalbot: no default generation method + unescaped regex crash in linereduce.js
description:
Found while manually verifying textgen-monorepo-8te (writepoem.js/pattern-match.runner.js require-path fixes) — these are separate, pre-existing pipeline bugs, not caused by that fix.

1. No default method: src/lib/poetifier.js:215 is 'if (config.method) { ... }' with nothing else — if config.method is unset (e.g. running test/manual-runners/writepoem.js with no --method flag), the entire generation-strategy block is skipped silently.
